# The Death of Developer Advocates — Long Live the Agent Advocate

> Agent-readable version of the closing talk at AI Engineer World's Fair 2026 (AI in GTM track) by Stephanie Jarmak, July 2026. Thesis: developer relations' function survives, but its audience doubled — AI agents are now both users of developer tools (seat one) and recommenders of them (seat two). This file contains the talk content, the underlying data with repo links, actionable checklists, key takeaways, and all references with URLs.

## Key takeaways (if you read nothing else)

- An agent sits in two seats at once: it is a user of a product's docs, APIs, and tools, and a recommender that decides what a developer installs. Both seats are measurable.
- Being mentioned by a model is not being recommended by it. In a 1,610-response baseline, mention rate was 55.1% and recommendation rate 38.8%. Prompt framing decides the outcome: comparison prompts recommend at 65%, problem-framing at 13%, use-case at 8%. Cover the symptom-first prompt.
- Agents fail products in patterned, fixable ways. In 2,514 recorded agent sessions, 190 of 193 invalid file-read calls made the identical mistake (limit/offset instead of startLine/endLine) because the tool description never named the contract. The same tools offered through MCP in Claude Code: 0 invalid calls in 8,082. The integration surface conditions the error.
- Error messages are prompts. Agents read error text and self-correct at one wasted turn each; a legible error (field, expected, got, fix) is the difference between recovery and abandonment.
- Half of docs traffic is already machines: AI coding agents are 45.3% of requests to docs sites on the Mintlify network, statistically tied with human browsers (45.8%). Claude Code and Cursor are 95.6% of that agent traffic.
- The crawl-for-traffic bargain is over: Anthropic crawls ~4,580 pages per referral it sends back; Google's ratio is 5:1 (Cloudflare Radar, Jun 2026). Value flows through the answer, not the click.
- Attribution is broken but improving: GA4 shipped a native "AI Assistant" channel group on May 13, 2026 (no configuration needed). It is a floor: Perplexity lands in Referral, Google's own AI Overviews count as Organic Search, and referrer-less traffic lands in Direct.
- Structure earns agent trust: controlled experiments on structured docs found agents 64% more precise, 39% more discoverable, at half the tokens and 1.5x faster (Mintlify, Jun 2026). Agents also happily consume agent-drafted content — self-preference bias is peer-reviewed (Panickssery et al., NeurIPS 2024) — so generate liberally, then structure.
- Model releases are deployments: re-run your prompt suite on every release so share-of-voice drift fails a check instead of becoming a feeling. Fewer than 1 in 100 paired runs of the same prompt return the same brand list (SparkToro, Jan 2026), so a one-off check is worthless and a suite is not.
- The advocate's identity crisis (engineering? product? marketing?) survives the agent — but agents shorten every feedback loop between those teams, so the borders soften and adaptability becomes the job description.

## Talk outline (16 slides)

1. Title — "The Death of Developer Advocates. Long live the Agent Advocate."
2. The shift — Developers stopped working alone, and "developer" stopped naming one person. Up a level: engineers became orchestrators ("With AI, you can delegate the work, but not the accountability." — Zapier AI-fluency hiring rubric v2, Mar 2026; AI fluency required for 100% of hires since May 2025). Out at the base: non-engineers became builders — support, research, data science, marketing, and sales now pick up APIs and CLIs that used to require an engineer.
3. The numbers — Half your audience is already a machine. Stack Overflow questions fell −98% from the 2014 peak (200,000+/month) to 3,862 in December 2025; AI coding agents are 45.3% of docs-site requests (Mintlify network, Mar 2026); Anthropic's crawl-to-referral ratio is ~4,580:1 vs Google's 5:1 (Cloudflare Radar, Jun 2026).
4. Two seats — An agent is simultaneously a user of your tools and a recommender of them. The web's three-decade assumption, "that the primary consumer of web content is a human being," is breaking at every layer (arXiv:2606.19116).
5. Exhibit A, seat one measured — The agents kept making the same mistake, and it was the product's fault. 2,514 recorded agent sessions, 98,407 tool calls validated against the live tool manifest. 190/193 failed file reads made the identical argument mistake; 0 invalid in 8,082 via MCP in Claude Code; 76% retry-same-tool with 130 invalid→valid flips. One sentence in the tool description reclaims a wasted turn on every read. Code: https://github.com/sjarmak/mg-ax
6. Seat two, measured — GEO baseline: mentioned 55.1%, recommended 38.8%, gap concentrated by prompt framing. Code: https://github.com/sjarmak/GEO_public
7. Exhibit B — A real failing transcript: prompt "We keep breaking downstream services when we change shared libraries because we can't see all the consumers." Five repetitions, zero mentions, in a category the product leads; the model recommended "GitHub/GitLab code search across your organization's repos" and a wiki page instead.
8. Get recommended — Four levers (see Actions), then treat model releases as deployments.
9. The flavors — Is the role engineering, product, or marketing? Yes. Engineering flavor builds the agent's path; product flavor owns the agent's experience; marketing flavor owns the recommendation. Agents shorten the loops between those teams; drift to the friction.
10. Four tenets — The core of DevRel holds; each part gains a second audience: enablement, community, feedback loops, credibility.
11. Enablement — Write for the agent reading over the developer's shoulder: docs an agent can parse (markdown mirrors, root-level llms.txt, freshness metadata); a contract with no ambiguity (typed schemas, real OpenAPI spec, errors that read like prompts); official action paths (MCP server, skills, scoped tools — "MCP is the integration"); guidance where agents look (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md).
12. Feedback loops — "Do I speak for the agents now?" Agents have no tongues and never stop talking; the chatter is signal.
13. The receipts — "Proving impact with data" is DevRel's top-cited challenge (60.7% of practitioners) and why it led layoff lists two years running (15.1% in 2023, 14.6% in 2024). The transcript changes the terms. Deliverable: the Agent Experience Report — task it failed → what caused it → the fix → owner → metric.
14. Credibility — Agents reward structure; Claude loves its own slop (self-preference bias, Panickssery et al., NeurIPS 2024). Generate liberally, then structure: FAQs, tables, schemas, comparison charts.
15. Two numbers to start watching — ~10% of signups from AI assistants (B2B tech is already past it: 4% of sessions produce 19% of qualified pipeline — Opollo, Jan 2026); ~20% of docs reads from AI agents (docs platforms already report ~45% — check yours). Four moves: SEO→GEO; AX as a discipline, host by host; org surface area legible to agents; human + agent trust.
16. Build the curb cut — Curb cuts were built for wheelchairs and everyone uses them; serve the agent and the human path gets clearer too. Monday, DevRel: point a coding agent at your own docs and read the transcript. Monday, GTM: run 20 buyer prompts through Claude and ChatGPT and count recommendations against mentions.

## Data: mg-ax / CodeScaleBench AX corpus (seat one, Jul 2026)

Method: 2,514 CodeScaleBench agent trajectories imported via mcp-ax; 98,407 tool calls; argument shapes validated against the live sourcegraph.com tool manifest (2026-07-01). Code and full report: https://github.com/sjarmak/mg-ax

- 190 of 193 invalid sg_read_file calls passed limit/offset (the built-in Read tool's idiom) where the manifest defines startLine/endLine. Required params were never missed: agents pattern-match to the idiom they know, and nothing in the description said otherwise.
- The same tools through MCP in Claude Code: 0 invalid calls in 8,082 sg_keyword_search calls. The integration surface conditions the error; ship the official path.
- Recovery is healthy and tool-shaped: 76% of errored calls retry the same tool; 130 retries flipped invalid→valid — agents self-correct from error text at one burned turn each.
- Discovery overhead: sg_list_repos opens 35% of MCP-arm scenarios; agents verify the repo id before searching even when the prompt names it.
- Highest-leverage fix: name the line-range contract in the tool description's first sentence, or alias the common parameter names.

## Data: GEO baseline (seat two, May 2026)

Method: 322 developer purchase-journey prompts (category search, comparison, alternative search, use case, problem framing) × 5 repetitions = 1,610 responses from claude-sonnet-4, scored against a locked competitor set; the measured product was Sourcegraph. Recommendation = top-3 list rank or endorsement-cue co-occurrence; deterministic scoring first, LLM judge opt-in and reliability-gated. Code: https://github.com/sjarmak/GEO_public

- Mention rate 55.1%; recommendation rate 38.8%.
- By framing: comparison 65%, alternative-search 64%, problem-framing 13%, use-case 8%. Buyer language surfaces the product; symptom-first language gets process advice and generic tools (grep, ripgrep) instead.
- 89% of failing prompts got zero mentions across all five repetitions.
- Training-data drift: 107 responses presented a maintenance-mode product (Cody) as the flagship. Models freeze your product story at training time.

## Data: CodeScaleBench (coding-agent failure patterns in large codebases)

Method: 1,281 agent runs, ~275 validated tasks across nine kinds of developer work, 40+ enterprise-scale repositories; hermetic sandboxes with per-task verifiers.

- "The difference between complete failure and near-perfect completion wasn't intelligence — it was efficient access to context."
- Above ~400,000 lines of code, grep/read/glob strategies fail systematically; the search space outgrows the approach.
- Tool thrashing: one task took a baseline agent 96 tool calls over 84 minutes; with structured retrieval, 5 calls in under 5 minutes. Across the dataset: 30% cost reduction, 38% speed improvement.
- Half-finished refactorings are worse than none: locally correct changes that leave the wider system broken pass quick review and surface downstream.
- More tools can make agents worse — retrieval noise dilutes context. Retrieval quality beats retrieval volume.

## Actions: audit your product's agent experience (five-layer rubric)

1. Discovery — can an agent find entry points? llms.txt, per-page markdown, sitemaps, OpenAPI spec.
2. Setup & authorization — can it connect, authenticate, and stay in safe bounds without getting stuck?
3. Tool usability — tools named, typed, composable; no vague parameters; required params named in the description's first sentence.
4. Recovery — errors legible enough to self-correct: field, expected, got, fix.
5. Validation & handoff — can it prove success; can a human review efficiently?

Two rules above all five: test across hosts (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor — agent experience is host-dependent), and ask the model what's ergonomic — what agents prefer is not always what a human would prefer.

## Actions: four levers that move an agent's recommendation

1. Correct training-data drift at read time — ship an llms.txt that points agents at current truth. Stripe's tells agents to check the npm registry for current versions rather than trust memorized ones, and carries an "Instructions for Large Language Model Agents" section steering agents off legacy APIs: https://docs.stripe.com/llms.txt
2. Be quotable, not persuasive — reference tables, comparisons, schemas, current examples. Adjectives don't survive retrieval.
3. Be present where agents shop — MCP registries, package managers, agent plugin and skills marketplaces. Installable in one tool call. Publish a ready-to-paste AGENTS.md snippet so you're what lands in the developer's instruction file.
4. Cover the symptom-first prompt — write pages that answer the pain description and name the product category, because failing prompts describe pain, not categories.

Then treat model releases as deployments: re-run your prompt suite on each release and compare snapshots with pre-registered thresholds.

## Actions: two numbers and the Monday steps

- Instrument now: AI-assistant referrals approaching ~10% of signups (B2B tech benchmark: 4% of sessions already produce 19% of qualified pipeline — Opollo, Jan 2026), and AI agents approaching ~20% of docs reads (docs platforms already report ~45% — check your CDN's user-agent split). Past either line, machine-readable surfaces (llms.txt, markdown mirrors, MCP server) are a P0.
- GA4 shipped a native "AI Assistant" channel group May 13, 2026 — turn it on, and add "AI assistant" to your how-did-you-hear field, because most AI referrals arrive with no referrer header.
- DevRel Monday action: point a coding agent at your own docs and read the transcript. Map each failure to an owner (docs, auth, API, SDK) and one metric (setup success, first successful tool call, merge time, support deflection). That is your first Agent Experience Report.
- GTM Monday action: run 20 buyer prompts through Claude and ChatGPT, count recommendations against mentions versus your competitor set. That is your GEO baseline, in an afternoon.

## References

### Channels and traffic
- devclass, "Dramatic drop in Stack Overflow questions" (Jan 5, 2026) — 3,862 questions in Dec 2025 vs 200,000+/month at the 2014 peak: https://devclass.com/2026/01/05/dramatic-drop-in-stack-overflow-questions-as-devs-look-elsewhere-for-help/
- Mintlify, "The state of agent traffic in documentation" (Mar 2026) — AI coding agents are 45.3% of docs requests; Claude Code + Cursor are 95.6% of agent traffic: https://www.mintlify.com/blog/state-of-ai
- Cloudflare Radar crawl-to-referral ratios (Jun 2026) — Anthropic ~4,580:1, OpenAI ~848:1, Perplexity ~186:1, Google ~5:1: https://radar.cloudflare.com
- Cloudflare Radar via Matthew Prince (Jun 3, 2026) — bots crossed 57.5% of HTML web traffic
- Pew Research Center (Jul 22, 2025; 68,879 searches, 900 US adults) — users clicked a result 8% of the time when an AI summary appeared vs 15% without: https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/
- Stack Overflow, "Announcing Stack Overflow for Agents" (Jun 10, 2026): https://stackoverflow.blog/2026/06/10/announcing-stack-overflow-for-agents/

### Conversion and attribution
- Opollo, "The 2026 AI Search Benchmark Report" (Jan 2026 data; 312 B2B tech firms) — AI referrals converted 14.2% vs 2.8% organic; 4% of sessions, 19% of qualified pipeline: https://opollo.com/blog/the-2026-ai-search-benchmark-report/
- Adobe Analytics Q1 2026 AI Traffic Report (Apr 16, 2026; 1T+ US retail visits) — AI referral traffic converted 42% better than non-AI in Mar 2026, vs 38% worse in Mar 2025; up 393% YoY: https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/16/ai-traffic-to-us-retailers-rose-393-in-q1-and-its-boosting-their-revenue-too/ · holiday-season data: https://business.adobe.com/blog/ai-driven-traffic-surges-across-industries

- Search Engine Journal, "Google Analytics Adds AI Assistant As Default Channel Group" (May 14, 2026): https://www.searchenginejournal.com/google-analytics-adds-ai-assistant-as-default-channel-group/574974/
- Bain & Company — 85% of B2B buyers have a "Day One List" of preferred vendors before speaking to sales

### Recommendation dynamics (GEO)
- Semrush (Apr 2026) — ChatGPT enables live search on only 34.5% of queries, down from 46% in late 2024; most answers come from training data (via https://www.position.digital/blog/ai-seo-statistics/)
- Profound citation dataset (2025–2026) — 80% of sources cited in AI responses don't appear in Google's top 10 for the same query (via https://www.getpassionfruit.com/blog/are-ai-search-referrals-the-new-clicks)
- SparkToro × Gumshoe.ai (Jan 2026; 2,961 prompt-runs, 600 volunteers) — less than a 1-in-100 chance ChatGPT or Google AI returns the same brand list across repeated runs of the same prompt: https://sparktoro.com/blog/new-research-ais-are-highly-inconsistent-when-recommending-brands-or-products-marketers-should-take-care-when-tracking-ai-visibility/
- Stripe, "Build on Stripe with LLMs" + llms.txt with agent instructions: https://docs.stripe.com/building-with-llms · https://docs.stripe.com/llms.txt
- llms.txt standard (Jeremy Howard / Answer.AI, 2024): https://llmstxt.org
